findings.description: The 'data' bucket is declared with no ACL restriction, no public access block, and no restrictive bucket policy, and the in-file comment states it is public. Objects stored in it, including the customer master spreadsheet, may be readable by anonymous users.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so sensitive customer data in this bucket is stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so there is no guardrail preventing public ACLs or public bucket policies from being applied - which is precisely how this bucket becomes exposed.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this publicly exposed bucket would leave no S3 access-log audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted by an attacker cannot be recovered, weakening data integrity protection.

A customer master spreadsheet (likely PII) is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly readable 'data' bucket with no object-level kms_key_id or restrictive ACL, exposing sensitive records to unauthenticated retrieval.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial records stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial data, so there is no audit trail of object access.
The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could silently expose financial data publicly.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or permanently deleted with no recovery path or MFA-delete protection.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational data is stored without server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no record of who accessed objects in this bucket for audit or incident investigation.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against a future public ACL or bucket policy.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its datasets (frequently derived from sensitive records) are unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving it dependent solely on the private ACL to prevent public exposure.
The centralized log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; combined with the log-delivery-write ACL, an accidental public policy or ACL change would expose aggregated access logs.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket, with no MFA delete or object lock, permits the entire log store and its version history to be wiped, destroying forensic evidence of an intrusion.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached to this or any other bucket in the file, so objects and logs may be transmitted over cleartext HTTP.
